title: Hermetic vertical journey: ready through accept over production wiring
description: Operator-ratified 2026-08-05, endorsed by two external adversarial review rounds; migration rule 4 sanctions it. Drive ready, assign, launch, report, evidence, handoff, accept through PRODUCTION composition and use-case wiring over the canonical fakes: FakeWorkProvider or scripted BrWorkProvider, InMemoryState with ManualClock (landed 7ef29e2), and the gyh.1 fake runtime peer. The test must invoke production wiring, never implement a second orchestration path inside itself. Deliberately small - exactly four paths: one complete happy path; one worker interruption or stale-attempt path; one Directive or abort path; one Acceptance or application-ambiguity path. Module suites keep all combinatorial cases; this journey proves the modules compose as a machine, not their individual contracts. Placement: prefer a dedicated dev-only integration crate so no production crate gains a lateral dependency; decide at cross-review. Rationale: three port-implementability gaps in one day (9nh.12, 9nh.13, constant-stub retirements) were invisible to text review and obvious under implementation pressure; this broadens that pressure from the state seam to composition. Test spec: new dev-only integration crate with four journey tests, hermetic, within workspace budget.
notes: 2026-08-05 placement and guardrails, BOTH reviewers aligned (Codex ACK + SABLE reviewer PASS): named leaf crate abacus-usecase-journeys, publish=false, test targets only; dev-dependencies inward on core/work/state/runtime; no production crate depends back; instantiates canonical fakes and calls abacus_core::usecase production functions. The driver may supply inputs, clocks, scripts, assertions; it may NOT own transition policy, receipt choice, retry/compensation rules, or direct state shortcuts. Helpers stay private and literal - no reusable orchestration DSL, no broad fixture package, no integration-common crate. Exactly the four pinned tests; new combinatorics go to owning module suites unless an existing journey's end-to-end semantic changes; cargo test --workspace includes the leaf, owning-package edit loops do not. PATH FOUR TIGHTENED (SABLE reviewer follow-up 3, supersedes any Acceptance-OR-ambiguity reading): one exact sequence - commit Acceptance, close application returns ambiguous, projection remains pending, EXPLICIT reconciliation observes/applies the effect, receipt clears pending. A happy Acceptance alone proves the easy half and misses the seam this journey exists to pressure. Recovery cases are NOT journeys: bind-or-stop compensation is pinned in the core usecase suite (see launch-association recovery bead), crash/restart in the transport lane - the four paths do not grow.
close_reason: All four pinned journey paths land and pass, driving production composition end to end over the canonical fakes. Path 1 happy: ready selection with the advice gate applied and its disposition surfaced, Assignment opening bound to the exact selected snapshot, mark-in-progress projected under the same authorizing operation, nothing left pending. Path 2 stale-attempt: revoke-then-append (the real sequence - a successor cannot open while its predecessor is active), predecessor's further write refused, successor unaffected. Path 3 Abort: in-band refusal naming the binding Abort with the response envelope still delivered, explicit compliance as the only terminal carrier, idempotent on replay, audited under a recovered worker binding; plus the inverse - no Abort means compliance is refused, so voluntary self-cancellation stays unrepresentable. Path 4 acceptance-ambiguity, exact reviewer-tightened sequence: evidence, Handoff submission, Acceptance committed, ambiguous close application, projection stays pending, explicit reconciliation under a fresh attempt identity, receipt clears. Crate placement per both lineages' ACK: named test-only leaf abacus-usecase-journeys, publish=false, dev-deps inward only, no production reverse edge, private literal helpers, no DSL or shared fixture package. FOUND BY THE JOURNEY, which is what it was for: abacus-gf6 (fenced call on an ended Attempt returns IncoherentBundle instead of a distinct supersession refusal - Codex has folded it into its C3 state pass, defaulting to StaleFencing), abacus-8tu (no production seam pairs revoke/reclaim with runtime stop), and two imagined sequences corrected against production rules (successor-while-predecessor-active; accepting a Handoff that was never submitted). Gates at close: 20 targets, 258 tests green, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean.

title: Planning and delivery architectural exams: admission criteria
description: Operator-ratified 2026-08-05; deferred constraint record, not current work. When the planning layer (sable-plan behavioral port) and the delivery layer are designed, they sit these exams. PLANNING: consumes existing facade state (work reads, state queries, decision records, audit) by default; any new durable planning fact - approval dossier, versioned design artifact, assessment receipt - requires a named owner and an ADR, a constraint not an absolute ban; planning policy never alters execution lifecycle semantics for convenience; if adding planning requires expanding the Assignment lifecycle, planning-specific Ledger tables without that ADR, or teaching every module about planning substages, the seams were shaped too narrowly and that finding outranks shipping the feature. DELIVERY: consumes accepted Handoffs; may own its own publication lifecycle states such as publication-attempted, integrated, deployed; never redefines Acceptance; does not pull GitHub, merge, CI, or deployment concepts into core. title: FakeState::record_application_receipt mutates before conflict detection
description: The in-memory WorkflowStatePort fake in abacus-core/src/ports.rs pushes the decision id onto self.receipts BEFORE calling self.apply, so a same-operation conflicting receipt (different after-revision) returns ConflictingOperation while having already cleared that decision from the derived pending_applications set. Same validate-then-commit defect class as the activation/opening/deactivation fixes in the credential follow-up, but outside that scope. Fix: compute key and content, check idempotency and conflict first, then push the receipt and commit together. Add a regression asserting a conflicting receipt leaves the decision in pending_applications. Test file is the ports.rs test module; run cargo test -p abacus-core plus clippy -D warnings and fmt.
close_reason: Validated current receipt path is validate-then-commit; added regression proving a refused revision-mismatched receipt leaves the projection pending. Core tests and clippy pass.

title: Credential carriage redesign: sandbox-scoped per-attempt credential file replaces context-held secrets
description: Operator directive 2026-08-05, superseding the compaction-loss doc-fix finding on ADR-0003: message-injected credentials held in agent context are rejected - context compaction can silently destroy a worker's ability to authenticate, and per-call reproduction from memory is fragile. Required shape (pending adversarial review and probes): the host-side launch composer writes the transient secret to a per-attempt file under the runtime directory (never the worktree; deleted at attempt end aligning with revocation); each worker's sandbox profile - which ABACUS configures at launch - grants read access to EXACTLY its own credential file (Codex permission-profile filesystem read scoping, Claude harness deny-rule equivalent); scribe-rpc's public envelope accepts the credential BY REFERENCE (well-known deterministic path re-derivable from cwd) and the composer reads the file host-side; agent context carries zero secret material. SECURITY ANALYSIS REQUIRED (the trap): a same-uid-readable file lets project-supplied verification commands harvest ALL workers' credentials - fleet impersonation - so sandbox read-scoping is the load-bearing control; without it exposure widens from live-window memory capture to at-rest file theft. Cross-worker theft blocked by scoping; own-worker project-code theft reduced to one credential bounded by lease fencing plus revocation, equivalent to today's accepted residual. GATES: compatibility probe proving per-path read scoping on BOTH harnesses (Codex profile filesystem policies; Claude deny rules) - HPG-style disposable evidence; ADR-0003 amendment rewriting the credential-carriage section and residuals; fallback same-uid-readable file requires explicit operator acceptance of the widened residual. Touches: launch composition abacus-core/runtime (Claude lane), scribe-rpc composer schema (Codex lane), role cards, docs/compatibility. ADR-0003 sign-off is PAUSED until the amended text is presented to the operator. Test spec: composer writes/deletes file at open/end (unit); scope-refusal probe rows (compatibility record); credential-by-reference round trip in the composer contract; context-free reauthentication scenario in the journey or module suite.
notes: 2026-08-06 SIGNED. The operator approved ADR-0003 revision 6 as written, which is the binding text for this bead's locked shape. Acceptance terms recorded on abacus-hpg.7: approved on the understanding that implementation contact may produce findings, which should amend the ADR rather than be worked around. This bead's design work is COMPLETE; it closes when both lanes' implementing diffs land (Codex: trait split, credential removal, locator resolution, gf6 stale-fencing; Claude: worker-trait-only composition refinement).

title: Ending an Attempt must sequence its runtime teardown: no production seam pairs revoke/reclaim with stop
description: Found 2026-08-06 by an operator question against the abacus-3ju journey: when an Attempt ends, who stops the agent process. VERIFIED GAP: abacus-core/src/usecase.rs contains no use case that sequences a terminal Attempt decision with RuntimePort::stop and the runtime-handle unbind - the only stop references are doc comments and a test fake. So today an orchestrator must remember to (a) record the Revoke/Reclaim decision and (b) separately stop the runtime session and unbind its handle, with nothing enforcing the pairing. That is exactly the remember-to-also-do-X rule that rots, and its failure mode is a live predecessor process running against a worktree whose Attempt the Ledger has already ended. WHY FENCING IS NOT SUFFICIENT ALONE (and why this is hygiene, not correctness): fencing already refuses the zombie's writes, so no corruption is possible - but leaving the process alive burns a pane, may keep editing the worktree, can consume provider quota, and produces confusing operator-visible state. Conversely the stop is NOT a substitute for fencing: RuntimePort::stop returns EffectReport::Applied or Ambiguous, an orchestrator can die between decision and stop, and CONTEXT section 5 makes runtime observations non-authoritative - so correctness must never depend on the process actually being dead. Both layers are required and neither replaces the other. SHAPE (small, and scoped to what journey path 3 needs - do NOT grow this into a lifecycle subsystem): a composition use case that records the terminal decision FIRST (the Ledger is authoritative), then stops the bound runtime session, then unbinds the handle, returning explicit typed outcomes for the stop - Applied, Ambiguous, or no bound handle - so an ambiguous stop is surfaced to the caller as an unresolved runtime condition rather than swallowed. Never a hidden retry (I12). Relates to abacus-bpr, which covers the LAUNCH side (bind-or-stop after an uncertain launch); this is the TEARDOWN side. Compare-and-swap unbind semantics from that bead apply here too: unbinding must not erase a newer valid association. TEST SPEC: usecase suite proves decision-then-stop ordering, that a failed or ambiguous stop still leaves the decision committed and surfaces the ambiguity typed, and that no bound handle is a typed outcome rather than an error; journey path 3 (Abort) drives the sequence end to end.
close_reason: Teardown seam implemented as end_attempt in abacus-core/src/usecase.rs. ORDER IS THE CONTRACT: the terminal decision (Revoke or Reclaim) commits FIRST - which is what makes a successor Attempt legal and instantly makes the predecessor's writes refusable - and only then is the bound session stopped and its association removed. Typed input AttemptEnd restricted to Revoke/Reclaim (S2 mirror of AcceptanceDecision): Accept has its own saga and Cancel ends every Attempt of an Assignment, so neither is expressible at this single-Attempt teardown. FOUR TYPED OUTCOMES, no hidden retries: ToreDown (stopped and unbound); StopAmbiguous keeping the association BOUND and surfacing the handle, because unbinding on an unknown stop would discard the only handle to a session that may still be running; StopFailed likewise bound with the normalized reason; NoRuntimeAssociation for an Attempt that ended before it ever launched, which is normal rather than an error. The decision stands committed in every variant - a failed or unknown reap must never un-end an Attempt, since the Ledger is authoritative and fencing already refuses a zombie's writes (CONTEXT section 5: runtime observations are non-authoritative, so correctness never depends on the process being dead; teardown is hygiene layered on that guarantee, never a substitute). FOUR TESTS red-first: ordering plus decision content; ambiguous stop keeps the binding; failed stop leaves the Attempt ended; no-association contacts no provider. KNOWN GAP NAMED IN CODE, not papered over: unbind_runtime_handle takes only the subject, so a re-association landing between the handle read and the unbind would be erased; compare-and-swap unbind arrives with abacus-bpr (Codex lane, post-ADR-signature) and this sequence adopts it then - the window is narrow because the Attempt is already terminal, but it is real. Gates: 20 targets, 267 tests green, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean. Pure composition, no state-seam or abacus-state changes.

title: Graph-authoring interface: split create/update/dependency from execution WorkGraphPort; no generic reopen
description: SABLE reviewer verdict 4 plus follow-up 4 (2026-08-05). Rescopes the abacus-omw epic Notes carry-forward ('WorkGraphPort needs the contract dependency/create/update/reopen surface'). DECIDED: do NOT widen the execution WorkGraphPort into a br CRUD mirror - it serves ready selection and decision projections, and widening it makes every execution fake and consumer implement planning authoring verbs, recreating core fan-out and C3 churn. Planning and CLI consume a SEPARATE graph-authoring interface owned with abacus-work's normalized vocabulary: explicit authority, expected graph revision, idempotency identity, typed fields, unambiguous requirement-direction dependency edits. Add it only when its real planning consumer arrives (ADR-0001 section 11 discipline). GENERIC REOPEN IS REJECTED, twice-evidenced: SABLE's sable-spawn-worker added reopen specifically so respawn could mutate a CLOSED bead back to in_progress to get runtime repair past tracker claim logic - coupling session recovery to work completion state, exactly the interweaving ABACUS removes; and providers.lock records reopen was intended only for explicit out-of-band-close reconciliation. ABACUS model stands: rejection or retry creates a new Attempt under the active Assignment; accepted and cancelled work is terminal; further work is a successor bead with a dependency. If an operator correction of a mistaken close is ever required it is a separate exceptional use case with Ledger-coherence checks, exact revision and authority, explicit audit, and NO intermediate ready window - never a routine planning verb, never part of projection reconciliation (if retained at all it lives only inside the explicit divergence-repair use case of the application-resolution work). BLOCKED by design until the planning consumer exists - deferred at creation.

title: Fenced worker calls cannot link Directive responses
description: WorkflowStatePort promises that immutable call ordering and linked responding actions derive Directive discharge, and every fenced response must surface the current binding set. The current seam cannot express the worker half: FencedCall has no responds_to SignalId and none of fenced_report, fenced_evidence, fenced_submit_handoff, or renew_lease accepts equivalent typed response metadata. Only DecisionRecord can link a decision. The core test FakeState masks this by returning a constant empty binding_directives set and never recording ResponseAction::WorkerAction. Before the abacus-state fake or SQLite implementation can honestly satisfy the contract, make the linkage representable (likely optional typed response metadata in the fenced call identity, but decide under C2/C3 discipline), persist it in causal order, and add portable regressions proving an unlinked action leaves Amend/Answer binding, a linked later action discharges exactly its target, replays do not duplicate ordering, and every fenced response returns the causally current binding set.
design: ADR-0001 Decision 8 amended 2026-08-05. FencedAction wraps FencedCall plus optional responds_to and is accepted only by fenced_report, fenced_evidence, and fenced_submit_handoff; renew_lease remains bare FencedCall. The link participates in full idempotent identity. Some must target an already-committed Directive for the same Assignment/Attempt; unknown and incoherent targets refuse without a commit. Permitted substantive actions enter causal ResponseAction order; domain-refused Handoffs own their audited outcome and advance call order but cannot discharge. Fenced responses derive post-commit current bindings/head, including replay without allocating another position.
notes: Implemented in the live tree with 5 new causal regressions. Core: 93 tests pass and strict all-target Clippy clean. Full C3 fan-out: 167 workspace tests, strict workspace all-target Clippy, fmt, and diff checks clean. Claude lineage issued C3 PASS with zero findings and explicitly confirmed current-on-replay semantics, refusal/action asymmetry, validation no-commit behavior, renewal exclusion, and transactional candidate-seq gate semantics. Carry these exact expectations into the shared WorkflowStatePort contract suite for 9nh.11 and the SQLite transaction tests for 9nh.10.
close_reason: Landed in c982cf8: ADR-0001 Decision 8 amendment, FencedAction response-link seam, causal FakeState derivation, and five regressions; Claude C3 cross-review PASS and full workspace gates green.

title: Abort gate cannot return response-bearing append refusals
description: Core and architecture require every validly fenced response to surface current binding Directives and require Abort to refuse further substantive worker mutations, but WorkflowStatePort::fenced_report and fenced_evidence can express refusal only as outer StateError, which carries no FencedResponse. The current fake therefore commits post-Abort Report/Evidence appends, while an opaque Err would strand the worker without the binding Abort. Add concrete in-band Recorded/Refused outcome types for Report and Evidence, always paired with FencedResponse; add one core append gate that refuses only AbortInForce. A refused append is an audited operation-owned outcome that advances call order, records no WorkerAction or payload, replays idempotently, and surfaces the causally current binding set. Renewal remains allowed after Abort so lease machinery can surface the instruction; Pause/Amend do not gate Report/Evidence; Handoff retains its existing all-kinds gate. Record the abort-consistent terminal action carriage or explicit deferral to 9nh.10. C2 ADR-first under a second dated ADR-0001 Decision 8 amendment; C3 full fan-out and Claude cross-review.
design: ADR-0001 Decision 8 amendment: ReportOutcome and EvidenceOutcome each distinguish Recorded from Refused { AbortInForce } while remaining paired with FencedResponse. A pure worker-append gate refuses only binding Abort; Pause and Amend remain appendable, Handoff keeps its stricter gate, and renewal is exempt as lease/discovery machinery. Fence/link/draft validation runs first and claims nothing on failure. A gate refusal owns the operation, advances causal call order, stores no payload or WorkerAction, and replays its stored outcome with the current envelope. The terminal abort-consistent carrier is an explicit 9nh.10 obligation.
acceptance_criteria: ADR and module contracts name the outcome, validation order, renewal exception, and 9nh.10 deferral. Both report and evidence refuse post-Abort in-band with Abort present in FencedResponse; no payload or WorkerAction commits; causal head advances. Exact replay is AlreadyApplied, duplicates nothing, and returns the current envelope; changed identity conflicts. Pause/Amend allow both appends. Renewal succeeds post-Abort and surfaces it. Invalid link post-Abort is an outer no-commit error and leaves the operation reusable. Core and full-workspace tests, strict clippy, fmt, diff check, and Claude C3 cross-review pass.

title: Projection resolution: causal supersession and the application-resolution disposition record
description: SABLE reviewer verdict 1 (2026-08-05, operator-relayed): BLOCKS INTERFACE FREEZE. Two cases are collapsed by the rule 'pending = projection lacking receipt' (abacus-state pending_applications derivation; ADR-0001 effect-provenance amendment at d4b5442). CASE A, causal supersession: an unconfirmed MarkInProgress projection whose Assignment later gets a COMMITTED terminal Accept/Cancel decision will redrive against the now-closed bead into FoundBeforeSubmission and ConflictingEffect forever, with no out-of-band actor involved. Repro path: assign_ready with ambiguous mark projection, then accept_handoff commits and its close applies, then redrive_pending re-drives the mark (abacus-core/src/usecase.rs project_pending; abacus-state/src/memory.rs projections map - nothing removes the nonterminal sibling). Fix: the later terminal projection causally supersedes the earlier nonterminal projection as a DERIVED Ledger fact - the actionable pending set becomes 'lacking receipt AND not causally superseded'; no fake receipt, no human waiver; superseded items stay queryable. CASE B, true external divergence (wrong close reason, unknown close, deletion, other provider mutation): add ONE immutable application-resolution record, separate from Assignment lifecycle DecisionKind, binding the target projection operation, the exact observed status and revision, a closed disposition enum plus bounded reason, a NEW operation identity, and the resolving authority. Authority is the Assignment's CURRENT decision authority under a dedicated reconciliation capability and scope; the pre-listen operator recovery channel is the only override. A typed Request may summon the decision but never discharges anything. Resolution removes the item from the actionable retry set (attention loop stops ringing) while staying queryable as a resolved divergence in audit and doctor. It never rewrites the original decision and never masquerades as an ApplicationReceipt. NOTE: the reviewer's Scribe backstop (refuse receipts whose attempt observed status does not satisfy the stored WorkProjection) was reviewed at 5d2327d and is SUBSUMED by the amendment's only-Applied receipt eligibility - implementation must confirm receipt validation refuses ALL non-Applied attempts. Approach: revise the cross-review-pending ADR-0001 amendment (supersession joins the pending-set doctrine; the resolution record is its own amendment block, reviewer-specified shape above). Lane split per amendment: derivation and storage Codex, core record vocabulary plus composition resolution use case Claude. Test spec: portable state contract proves terminal-decision commit removes the nonterminal sibling from the actionable set and proves resolution-record round-trip plus authority refusals; usecase suite proves the resolution use case retires the item from the retry set without receipt.
notes: 2026-08-05 update: CASE A (causal supersession) is now DOCTRINE in the ADR-0001 effect-provenance amendment at 0d18802, per Codex's five-point requirement folded in before its PASS: actionable pending excludes causally superseded; only v1 supersession = MarkInProgress followed in Ledger order by a committed Close projection for the same Assignment (Accept/Cancel only), superseded_by recorded, derivation from committed Ledger projection order only; derived disposition, both operations preserved; query shape = pending_applications actionable + sibling superseded_applications; supersession precedes receipt_candidate (no mutation/attempt/receipt); memory/SQLite/portable parity. This bead's remaining scope is therefore: CASE A implementation (Codex lane: derivation, superseded_applications query, portable contract; Claude lane: composition respects supersession in reconcile/redrive) and CASE B (true-divergence application-resolution record) which per the amendment text arrives by ITS OWN amendment before the state seam freezes - that amendment draft is the next design act on this bead. V1c confirmed both lineages: Scribe refuses ALL receipts naming any non-Applied outcome.

title: Launch-association recovery: durable LaunchIntent, idempotent rebind-or-stop, compare-and-swap unbind
description: SABLE reviewer verdict 2 (2026-08-05): BLOCKS v1 recovery paths. Three defects at 5d2327d. FIRST: usecase.rs LaunchSequenceOutcome::LaunchedUnbound OVERCLAIMS - StateError::Unavailable does not prove the bind transaction failed to commit, so association state is UNKNOWN, not definitely unbound; rename accordingly. The recovery sequence to pin as a core use case: reissue the SAME bind operation identity with the SAME subject and handle once Scribe is reachable; then inspect the durable association via runtime_handle(subject); same handle means recovered; a DIFFERENT handle means preserve the existing association and stop the newly launched handle; a definite refusal with no binding means stop the known handle; an ambiguous stop remains an explicit unresolved runtime condition (observe and escalate; for a worker subject the decision actor fences or revokes the Attempt before any successor launch). NEVER launch a second session for the same subject or correlation while unresolved. SECOND: WorkflowStatePort::unbind_runtime_handle names only the subject, so a stale repair can erase a NEWER valid association; any unbind used for reconciliation needs compare-and-swap semantics against the handle it believes it is removing (state seam change, Codex lane). THIRD, restart hole: LaunchCorrelation is pre-known only in caller memory - free-form, and the Ledger persists Envelope and post-success handle but not correlation, so a caller crash after provider launch and before binding leaves a live CREDENTIALED session undiscoverable by Scribe or the future attention module. Fix per ADR decision: persist a pre-launch LaunchIntent record (subject plus correlation) before any provider contact, OR make correlation a structurally enforced deterministic derivation from durable subject facts - the current ports.rs comment is not that proof. ADR-first: C2 on the state seam (CAS unbind, LaunchIntent record). Test spec: abacus-core usecase suite pins bind-or-stop compensation across all five outcomes with scripted state and runtime fakes; the process-crash and restart window is pinned in the later transport/composition lane, explicitly NOT as a fifth abacus-3ju path (reviewer: making every recovery case a root journey recreates SABLE broad-suite growth).

title: Fenced call on an ended Attempt or terminal Assignment returns IncoherentBundle instead of a distinct supersession refusal
description: Found by the abacus-3ju journey path 2 (stale-attempt rejection) on 2026-08-06 - exactly the class the journey exists to surface, invisible to module-level review because each layer looked correct alone. DEFECT: abacus-state/src/memory.rs:303-304 - the fenced-call validator returns StateError::IncoherentBundle when the Assignment is terminal or the Attempt is ended. IncoherentBundle's own documented meaning is 'a transactional bundle's identities disagree (e.g. the Assignment named by its authorizing decision differs from the Assignment record)'. A revoked or reclaimed worker issuing a perfectly well-formed Report has NO disagreeing identities; it has simply been superseded. WHY IT MATTERS: CONTEXT section 6 requires normalized state failures to be loud AND DISTINCT, and the two situations demand opposite worker responses - superseded means stop, preserve the worktree, your successor owns the work, do not retry; malformed bundle means your request construction is buggy and retrying identically will fail forever. A worker cannot currently tell them apart, so a correct worker cannot take the correct action. This also hits the honest-audit goal: the refusal reason recorded for a superseded write is misleading. REPRO (now pinned green-with-a-note in abacus-usecase-journeys/tests/stale_attempt.rs): open an Assignment, worker reports under token 1, orchestrator records a Revoke decision ending attempt 1, orchestrator appends the successor attempt under token 2, then the predecessor reports again under token 1 - observe Err(IncoherentBundle) where a supersession-specific refusal belongs. SUGGESTED FIX (Codex lane, abacus-state plus possibly a StateError variant in core): either reuse StaleFencing when the presented token belongs to an ended Attempt (defensible - the token IS stale), or add a distinct variant such as AttemptEnded/AssignmentTerminal if the taxonomy should separate 'your token is old' from 'your Attempt is over'. Prefer whichever keeps the closed set small; a new core variant is C3. TEST SPEC: portable state contract case asserting the distinct refusal for (a) revoked attempt, (b) reclaimed attempt, (c) terminal assignment, each with a well-formed fenced call; plus tighten the journey assertion in abacus-usecase-journeys/tests/stale_attempt.rs from is_err to the exact variant once chosen. NOT BLOCKING: the write IS refused today, so no corruption or double-write is possible - this is a diagnosability and taxonomy-honesty defect, not a correctness hole.

title: Attention service: ADR and deterministic liveness module (doorbell as required product layer)
description: Operator decision 2026-08-05: a reliable doorbell is non-negotiable v1 product scope, elevated from optional convenience per the SABLE reviewer's brief. The I12 boundary reading already sanctions the shape: an explicitly authorized operations module arriving by its own ADR - this bead is that ADR plus the module epic it opens. Required split: Ledger/Scribe owns durable obligation and authority; the attention service owns reliable attention; Herdr owns delivery; only substantive workflow action resolves anything. Semantics: at-least-once content-free attention, never exactly-once or read semantics; durable fact commits first; ring only on state change with query-Scribe as the payload; duplicates harmless; provider Submitted never means read or resolved; ringing stops only when the actionable condition disappears through workflow state. The service is DETERMINISTIC ORDINARY SOFTWARE for the reliability floor - never solely an LLM watchdog that can itself idle - deriving attention obligations from unresolved Signals, pending Handoffs, ready work, and reclaimable leases; resolving generation-fenced runtime handles; recording Submitted/NotDelivered/Ambiguous delivery attempts for diagnosis and throttling, with that metadata separate from Signal semantics and never claiming read, understanding, discharge, or resolution; bounded-backoff re-ring; visible escalation on missing runtime or prolonged inaction. Agents may add judgment above the floor. I12 stays coherent: kernel correctness survives service absence, but safe-when-absent does not mean optional-to-ship. Critical proofs for acceptance: crash after Signal commit before ring recovers on restart; duplicate and ambiguous deliveries are harmless and retried; stale generations never target the wrong Attempt; Herdr or service outage catches up; absent sessions recover, launch, or escalate per policy; unresolved state keeps bounded re-ring despite Submitted; resolved state stops ringing without any mutable ack. Consumes existing runtime and state seams; any new state query surface (reclaimable leases, pending Handoffs) is named in the ADR. Passes the core-admission test as an outer module.
design: ADR-0004 written 2026-08-06 (docs/adr/0004-attention-service.md), Proposed pending Codex cross-review. Operator decisions taken in the planning session, all four: (1) both audiences, split by condition, each obligation declaring its own audience so routing is data not branching; (2) NOTHING remembered between runs - the tick interval is the rate limit and urgency is arithmetic on durable timestamps; (3) the recurring tick is EXTERNAL to ABACUS, so I12 stays literally true and no ABACUS-owned loop exists; (4) three obligation classes - unresolved Signals, pending Handoffs, reclaimable leases - with ready-work-without-worker EXPLICITLY EXCLUDED as scheduling rather than attention. The design deliberately cuts three of the heaviest items in this bead's original brief rather than deferring them: per-obligation backoff state, the escalation ladder, and a delivery-attempt store. Each rationale is preserved by other means - pacing from the tick interval, urgency from durable record timestamps, diagnosis on the existing audit trail. Most of the acceptance proofs demanded here are then satisfied BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by machinery, which is the strongest argument for the shape: with no ring state there is nothing to lose in a crash, a duplicate nudge is a no-op, and a resolved obligation stops deriving with no ack to clear. Load-bearing safety property: the module is read-only with respect to workflow state and holds no authority - it can ring and report, nothing else. That is what satisfies the I12 boundary reading requirement that its absence or failure never corrupt or invent workflow state, and it means a stalled worker with no live session is escalated, never auto-recovered, because recovery is a fenced decision under I17.

Both return owned Vec, both carry the durable timestamp the derivation needs for age arithmetic (Handoff submission time, lease expiry time) since ADR-0004 section 3 computes urgency from those timestamps and stores nothing. Implement in abacus-state/src/sqlite.rs and memory.rs, and extend the shared harness in abacus-state/src/contract.rs so both backends prove identical behavior. notes: ADR-0004 revision 2 correction, read before implementing: HandoffRecord in abacus-core/src/ports.rs carries NO temporal field, and Signal carries only a Seq (commit order, not time). Only Lease has wall-clock (expires_at). So pending_handoffs() must return the record TOGETHER WITH its submission timestamp, joined in SQL from the creating audit event - I10 guarantees exactly one such event exists and AuditEvent carries at: Timestamp. The join belongs in abacus-state precisely because HandoffRecord has no seq, leaving the attention module no way to bound an audit query itself. reclaimable_leases(now) needs no join; expires_at is already on Lease. Unresolved Signals are NOT part of this bead - the module bounds its own audit query by the minimum seq among unresolved Signals, so unresolved_signals() keeps its current signature and no pre-existing seam changes shape.

title: abacus-attention: the pure derivation (no I/O, no state, no timers)
description: The whole correctness surface of ADR-0004, and the only part that must be exactly right. New crate abacus-attention, publish = false, depending on abacus-core ports only, depended on by nothing inward, so it passes the core-admission test as an outer module per ADR-0001. Add it to the workspace members in Cargo.toml and lock the package entry in Cargo.lock in the same commit. Implement one function shaped attention(state, work, now, policy) returning an AttentionReport of typed Obligations. It performs NO I/O, holds NO state, keeps NO clock (now is a parameter), and CANNOT mutate workflow state - ADR-0004 section 2 makes read-only the load-bearing safety property, so the signature must take only read traits and must never accept a writer. Three obligation classes per ADR-0004 section 5, each carrying its own audience: unresolved Signal (recipient, escalating to operator once aged past policy), pending Handoff (deciding actor, escalating once aged), reclaimable lease (operator unconditionally, because a presumed-dead worker cannot answer a doorbell and reclamation is a fenced decision). Every Obligation carries the age of the durable record that produced it, computed as a pure function of that record timestamp and now. AttentionPolicy holds the thresholds as ordinary values passed in; it is NOT a new config schema and introduces no file format. Ready work with no worker is deliberately EXCLUDED - operator decision, that is scheduling not attention. Test spec: unit tests in the crate against fabricated state with no I/O, covering per class that the obligation derives when owed, does not derive once the linked responding action exists, and is promoted to operator-class exactly at the threshold and not one tick before; plus a determinism case asserting two runs over unchanged state produce an identical report.
notes: ADR-0004 revision 2 correction: age is NOT readable off the records. Signal carries only Seq and HandoffRecord carries no temporal field; only Lease has expires_at. Per ADR-0004 section 3 the derivation gets commit time from the audit trail, which I10 guarantees exists with at: Timestamp on every AuditEvent. For unresolved Signals the module does the join itself - read unresolved_signals(), take the minimum Signal.seq, then one audit_events query with AuditQuery { class: Some(AuditClass::Signal), from: Some(min_seq), .. } and join by the signal id carried on AuditKind (DirectiveAppended, RequestAppended, ReportRecorded). The seq bound is what keeps that query from growing with project history. Handoff and lease timestamps arrive pre-joined from abacus-ikq.1 and need no work here. Age derivation carries the test burden of the escalation ladder it replaced, so test promotion AT the threshold and one tick before it, per class.

title: abacus-attention: the ring pass, with delivery outcomes on the existing audit trail
description: The plumbing around the derivation from abacus-ikq.2. ADR-0004 section 6 forbids a new delivery store: that metadata is strictly diagnostic, is never read back by the derivation, never affects whether an obligation is owed, and never claims a Signal was read, understood, discharged, or resolved. HandleStale is EXPECTED during reclaim, is not an error, and must not abort the run - the remaining obligations still ring. Operator-audience obligations are always surfaced in the returned report, and additionally rung only if the operator has a live runtime handle; no new notification channel exists in v1 per ADR-0004 section 7. The pass still performs no workflow mutation. Test spec: an integration test driving real composition - real state, fake runtime peer, no network, no user home - asserting obligations derived, doorbells attempted, outcomes audited, and ZERO durable workflow mutations. That no-mutation assertion is the one this module cannot ship without. Plus a stale-handle case proving the run records HandleStale and completes remaining obligations, and an idempotence case proving a second pass over unchanged state changes no workflow state.

title: Launch eligibility gate: an opening's mark projection must be receipted or resolved before launch
description: SABLE reviewer follow-up tightening 2 (2026-08-05, seam trace at 5d2327d). An Assignment opening currently remains LAUNCHABLE even when its MarkInProgress projection returned Unresolved: nothing connects usecase::assign_ready's projection outcome to usecase::launch_subject's preconditions. That is the causal path by which a defer race or provider failure produces an active, credentialed worker while the work graph never confirmed in-progress. Fix in production composition (abacus-core/src/usecase.rs): before launching a WorkerAttempt subject, the composition must require the opening operation's projection to hold a successful receipt, or an explicit divergence resolution (see the application-resolution record bead) - returning Unresolved is recoverable state, not permission to proceed. Design note: the check needs the pending set (opening operation still pending means no receipt) - refuse with a typed in-band outcome naming the unconfirmed projection, mirroring AssignRefusal's pre-mutation refusal idiom; no hidden retry. Depends on the projection-resolution bead for the resolved-divergence alternative but the receipt-required gate can land first with resolution as a follow-on acceptance path. Test spec: usecase suite - launch refused while the opening operation is pending (typed refusal, zero state or runtime mutation, envelope NOT persisted); launch proceeds once the projection is receipted; later, launch proceeds when a resolution record covers the divergence.
close_reason: Launch eligibility gate implemented in production composition (abacus-core/src/usecase.rs, launch_subject). A worker Attempt may not be launched while its Assignment opening's mark-in-progress projection is still in the actionable pending set - that unconfirmed window is the causal path by which a defer race or provider failure produces an active worker while the work graph never recorded the work as started. Returning Unresolved is recoverable state, not permission to proceed. SHAPE: the gate is checked FIRST, before the Envelope is persisted and long before any provider contact, and refuses in-band with a typed LaunchRefusal rather than an error - mirroring AssignRefusal's pre-mutation idiom. Two refusal reasons: ProjectionUnconfirmed{operation} when the opening is still pending, and MissingWorkerOpening when a worker launch does not name the gating operation at all - omission is a REFUSAL, not a bypass, because a gate a caller can skip by forgetting is not a gate. ActorActivation subjects have no work-graph projection and are unaffected. THREE TESTS, red observed first: unconfirmed projection refuses with zero durable writes and zero provider contact; a missing opening refuses rather than waving through; a confirmed projection permits the launch. The later resolved-divergence acceptance path (launch permitted once a resolution record covers the divergence) waits on abacus-bcm case B, as the bead anticipated - the receipt-required gate lands first and stands alone. Gates: 20 targets, 263 tests green, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean. Pure composition: no abacus-core state-seam type changes, no abacus-state changes, so no overlap with the Codex lane's post-signature touching set.

title: Durable operation identity: idempotent replay keys must survive total context loss
description: SABLE reviewer finding 2026-08-05, surfaced during the abacus-719 credential redesign but INDEPENDENT of it: even after credential carriage is repaired, the claim 'total context loss costs nothing' remains FALSE if a call's operation identity (idempotency key) exists only in the worker's conversation context. Concrete failure: a worker issues a fenced call, the response is lost, the outcome is Ambiguous - the correct recovery is an EXPLICIT reissue under the SAME operation id (ADR-0003 no-silent-retry doctrine, and the whole reason Ambiguous returns the same transient provisioning). If the worker compacts before reissuing, it has lost the idempotency key. It then either cannot reissue at all, or reissues under a FRESH operation id, which is a second distinct operation - exactly the double-apply the operation-identity design exists to prevent. Same class applies to any in-flight call identity a worker must retain across turns. REQUIRED (design not yet chosen): a worker must be able to recover its in-flight/unresolved call identities from durable state after total context loss - candidate shapes: the Envelope/current-binding recovery path returns unresolved operations for the Attempt (architecture.md:411 shows the Envelope already carries Assignment identity, Attempt identity, fencing token, edit scope, acceptance policy, supported commands - extend that recovery surface rather than inventing a second one), or Scribe exposes a derived per-Attempt in-flight/unacknowledged set analogous to unresolved_signals and pending_applications. Note the derived-set pattern is already the house idiom for exactly this. ACCEPTANCE ROWS from the reviewer: a genuine context-loss proof erases the ENTIRE conversation, not merely the bearer, and shows the worker can invoke ONE stable recovery command with no remembered ActorId, AttemptId, token, or secret; be authenticated; retrieve the canonical Envelope and current binding; and resume a fenced operation safely - PLUS the harder row, compaction DURING an ambiguous call remains safely recoverable. Depends on the abacus-719 boundary choice only insofar as the recovery command must itself authenticate; the durable-identity requirement stands regardless of which credential boundary is adopted.
